questions.question: Which events does the debugging guide list as important to log? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Startup steps
Resource access
Tool execution
Error conditions and performance metrics
Raw Authorization headers for reproduction

questions.explanation: Startup, resource access, tool execution, errors, and performance metrics are the list. Credentials must never be logged.

questions.question: A client fails to connect. Which steps are on the official connection-troubleshooting checklist? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Check the client's logs
Verify the server process is running
Test the server standalone with the MCP Inspector
Call server/discover to verify protocol compatibility
Flush the OS DNS cache as the first step

questions.explanation: Logs, process check, Inspector, and protocol verification via server/discover (plus inspecting the per-request _meta fields) are the documented steps. DNS flushing isn't part of the checklist.

questions.question: Which error-code interpretations from the 2026-07-28 debugging guidance are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersionError — the data field lists the server's supported versions
-32021 MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError — names client capabilities the server needs but the request didn't declare
-32602 Invalid params — also returned when a request is missing required _meta fields
-32020 HeaderMismatch — Streamable HTTP headers disagree with the body
-32700 — the server ran out of memory

questions.explanation: A–D are correct. -32700 is JSON-RPC's Parse error (invalid JSON), not an out-of-memory signal.

questions.question: Which statements about Claude Desktop's MCP logs are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: macOS location: ~/Library/Logs/Claude
Windows location: %APPDATA%\Claude\logs
mcp.log holds general connection logging
mcp-server-SERVERNAME.log captures each server's stderr output
Logs are only available with a paid plan

questions.explanation: Locations and file roles are as documented; logging is built in, not gated.

questions.question: Which are documented debugging workflows for a misbehaving local server? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Test it standalone in the Inspector before blaming the host integration
Tail ~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-NAME.log to read the server's stderr
Add stderr logging around startup, tool execution, and error paths
Add print() statements to trace the message flow on stdio
All of the above

questions.explanation: print() writes to stdout and corrupts the protocol stream — the one thing you must not do on a stdio server.

questions.question: Your modern client gets error -32021 from a server. Which statements apply? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The error is MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError
The server needs a client capability (possibly an extension) the request's _meta didn't declare
The fix is declaring the capability in io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities on each request
The error means the JSON was unparseable
All of the above

questions.explanation: -32021 is the capability-gap error in the MCP-reserved range; unparseable JSON is -32700.

questions.question: Which places surface MCP diagnostics in Claude Desktop? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: mcp.log for general connection events
mcp-server-NAME.log for a specific server's stderr
The Developer settings / tools UI showing server status
The macOS Console app is required to decrypt the logs
All of the above

questions.explanation: Logs are plain files under ~/Library/Logs/Claude (or %APPDATA%\Claude\logs) — nothing is encrypted.

questions.question: A dual-era server serves an old IDE plugin and a new agent. Which debugging expectations are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A legacy client's traffic starts with an initialize handshake and may carry no modern protocol header
A modern client's requests each carry protocol metadata in _meta and can hit any instance
The server routes per request, so both clients can share one deployment
Version negotiation automatically translates legacy requests into modern ones
All of the above

questions.explanation: Negotiation detects era, it doesn't bridge it — the server (or SDK) must actually implement both legs; nothing translates on the wire for free.
